title: Using CodeIgniter Models (Part 2)
description: A continuation of the Models introduction: calling a Model method, fetching rows with the query builder, and seeing Model, Controller, and View work together.
congratsText: You can now pull real data out of a Model and get it onto the page!
objectives: Call a Model method from a Controller and store the value it returns
Use $this->db->get() inside a Model to fetch rows from a table
Choose between result() and row() based on how many rows you expect
Trace how a Model, Controller, and View cooperate on one request
recap: A Model method returns data, and the Controller catches that value in a variable
$this->db->get('table') runs the SELECT and hands back a query object
result() gives many rows, while row() gives just one
The Model supplies data, the Controller directs traffic, and the View displays it

sections.title: Calling a Method, Catching the Return

chunks.text: Once a Model is loaded, you call its methods like this: $this->student_model->get_all().

check.question: How do you call a Model method?

chunks.text: A Model method returns its data back to the Controller — it does not print anything on its own.

check.question: Does a Model method echo its data?

chunks.text: The Controller catches that value in a variable, then puts it in $data to pass to a View.

chunks.text: Inside a Model you reach the database through $this->db, which CodeIgniter provides for you.

chunks.text: $this->db->get('students') runs a SELECT on the students table and hands back a query object.
